To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the portfolio allocation to xed income, fund size, and manager experience were the most relevant factors in explaining fund performance.

the best performing multimarket funds in the Brazilian market are those with less experience, that invest more in xed incomes, that are managed by less experienced managers and that have more funds under management.
the best risk-adjustent performance is delivered by multimarket funds that are managed by less experienced managers and invest more in xed-income securities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the performance of multimanager funds, and the impact of the characteristics of managers and portfolio allocation on fund performance, which are factors that have been overlooked in the literature.

the following issues: (1) whether the manager characteristics and portfolio composition can explain fund performance; (2) whether there is any evidence of a change in the performance in Brazilian multimarket funds in the postcrisis period, and (3) whether there are any di erences in multimarket fund performance between the pre- and postcrisis periods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multimarket funds that are less e ective, invest less in xed income and are managed by inexperienced managers tend to deliver higher riskadjusted returns.
multimarket fund managers in Brazil, who invest in a more xed income portfolio, and who have a smaller number of funds under management, have better risk-adjusted returns.

multimarket funds that are managed by less experienced managers and invest more of their assets in xed income are likely to deliver better performance than multimarket funds that have a greater proportion of variable income and are managed by more experienced managers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best performance is delivered by less experienced funds, investing more in xing income, and managed by managers with more funds, and larger funds.
the performance of Brazilian funds was a ected by the manager characteristics and by the allocation of portfolios to xed or liquid assets.
the best performance was achieved by managers with less than 10 years of experience, investing more than half of their portfolios in xed income and with more than 100 funds under management.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the portfolio composition and manager characteristics can explain a signi cant part of the di erences in performance of Brazilian multimatter funds.

, in the context of Brazilian multimarket investment funds, portfolio allocation is the main factor in explaining a possible change in fund performance, followed by fund size, the number of funds under management, the experience of the fund manager, and the fund age.

the manager and portfolio allocation characteristics can be used by investors in Brazil in order to select funds with better performance, which is an important issue for the development of capital markets in emerging countries.
